title: Enterprise capacity profile & SLA onboarding playbook
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable intake and triage playbook for enterprise Dedicated capacity requests that translates customer requirements into a concrete capacity profile (SLA targets, reserved throughput, GPU class, scaling policy) and an onboarding checklist for Sales/SEs. Current intake is ad-hoc, leading to mismatch between contracted SLA and deployed configuration.

Goals:
- Produce a deterministic mapping from customer requirements to: SLA targets (p99 latency, availability), reserved throughput (tokens/sec or concurrent requests), GPU class recommendation, and autoscaling policy parameters.
- Create an onboarding checklist (technical, security, billing) that reduces back-and-forth by >50% during sales handoff.
- Surface cost trade-offs with clear options for customers (lower cost vs stricter SLOs).

Context & Motivation:
Enterprise customers frequently request "dedicated capacity" but use different language for needs (e.g., "low latency chat", "streaming 2k tokens", "100 concurrent agents"). Sales and Solutions Engineering lack a concise decision tree to size deployments. The runtime/infra team sometimes chooses GPU tiers reactively, causing rework. This ticket captures PM work to create the playbook and a light-weight intake form for SEs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A one-page decision tree PDF that maps customer requirements to a capacity profile (SLA targets + recommended GPUs + reserved throughput metrics).
- An intake form template for SEs (Confluence + CSV) that collects canonical signals: peak qps, median/90/99 latency SLOs, payload token lengths, model family preference, data residency, burst patterns, budget constraints.
- A set of recommended default scaling policies (warm pool sizes, scale-up thresholds, burst capacity) for 3 customer archetypes (low-latency chat, high-throughput embedding, mixed workloads).
- Example offer templates (SLA language + operational responsibilities) for Legal/RevOps.

Proposed triage flow (high-level):
1) SE fills intake form during qualification call.
2) PM/Runtime on-call run quick-sizing exercise (30 min) using internal tools (cost model + perf profiles) to propose 2 sizing options: Performance-first and Cost-balanced.
3) Present options to customer + recommend GPU tier.
4) If customer signs, trigger Dedicated onboarding runbook, spin reserved capacity, schedule customer-facing readiness check.

SLA target recommendations (initial):
- Latency-focused profile: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms, Availability 99.95% (SLA).
- Balanced profile: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms, Availability 99.9%.
- Throughput-focused profile: throughput guarantees expressed as reserved tokens/sec or concurrency (e.g., 2M tokens/min sustained) with best-effort latency targets.

Reserved throughput units (proposal):
- Use "reserved tokens/sec" as canonical unit for language workloads and "reserved RPS" for short-request workloads.
- Map examples: 1 A100 with q4f16 quant model ~ 50k tokens/sec sustained (in our perf benchmarks); H100 baseline ~ 85k tokens/sec; T4 ~ 8-12k tokens/sec depending on sequence length.

GPU class guidance (initial mapping):
- H100: high-concurrency, highest throughput for FP16/AMP models and long-context streaming.
- A100: general-purpose high-throughput for most production text-gen large models.
- T4 / 80GB equivalents: cost-optimized for smaller models or low-throughput embedding-only workloads.
- Quantized CPU fallback: for ultra-low-cost minimal SLA (best-effort).

Scaling policy proposals (defaults):
- Warm pool: keep N spare GPUs (N = ceil(0.1 * reserved_pool_size), min 1) to handle sudden bursts.
- Scale up: trigger when sustained utilization > 70% for 30s; scale additional replicas in steps of 20% of reserved capacity.
- Scale down: cooldown 10m after last scale-up; do not scale below reserved baseline.
- Burst window: allow 20% temporary overprovisioning for up to 60s if budget allows; require customer opt-in for sustained bursts.

Trade-offs to call out:
- Lower latency targets require larger warm pools and higher cost due to idle capacity.
- GPU class choice affects not only latency/throughput but also model compatibility (some models perform better on H100 kernels).

- Quick-sizing spreadsheet (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/sizing-templates/Dedicated-QuickSize

Open questions (to resolve in discovery):
- Should we charge a "warm-pool reservation" fee or absorb as part of reserved capacity pricing? (Finance input required)
- Exact token/sec mapping by model variant needs validation from benchmarks on H100 vs A100 (action: Perf team to run 3 representative models).
- How to express multi-model workloads (customer wants 10% low-latency chat + 90% background embeddings) in the intake form?

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (this ticket): Build playbook, intake form, and two example templates.
- Phase 1: Pilot with 3 existing prospects, collect feedback, tune thresholds.
- Phase 2: Bake into onboarding automation and Console UI (capacity profile toggles).
